access_method: Official REST API with an API key (src/collect_youtube.py); search.list then videos.list then commentThreads.list; regionCode=IN
fields_collected: video id, title, channel id, published_at, view/like/comment counts; top-level comment id, text, like count, published_at
granularity: daily snapshot per product (counts are cumulative at collection time)
limitations: Default quota 10,000 units/day plus 100 search.list calls/day (each list call costs 1 unit); search results are a relevance-ranked sample, not all videos; like counts can be hidden; comments can be disabled; history is not available, so trends need repeated snapshots
terms_note: Subject to the YouTube API Services Terms of Service and Developer Policies (data storage and refresh rules apply); API key kept in .env and never committed

access_method: Manual CSV export from trends.google.com (Interest over time), saved untouched to raw/trends/ and parsed by src/load_trends.py
fields_collected: relative search interest (0-100) per date for one search term; India; Web Search; All categories
granularity: weekly for a 12-month window (daily for windows of 90 days or less)
limitations: Values are relative and rescaled per export (peak=100), so they are not absolute volumes; '<1' values stored as 0.5; low-volume terms return zeros; manual process, so settings must be kept identical
terms_note: Used under the Google Terms of Service via the public website; no scraping or unofficial APIs; cite Google Trends as the source

access_method: Manual CSV export from trends.google.com (Interest over time) with a custom time range, saved untouched to raw/trends/ and parsed by src/load_trends.py
fields_collected: relative search interest (0-100) per day for one search term; India; Web Search; All categories
granularity: daily; window changed on 2026-10-03 from 12 months weekly to a 269-day custom range (about 9 months), identical for every product; supersedes the earlier Google Trends row
limitations: Daily data is only returned for ranges of 269 days or less (secondary sources, not official docs); values rescaled per export (peak=100); '<1' stored as 0.5; loader rejects weekly or monthly files and mismatched date ranges
terms_note: Used under the Google Terms of Service via the public website; no scraping or unofficial APIs; cite Google Trends as the source
